$schema_note: Internal development/test reference only. Not a runtime dependency: never add this directory to packaging/plaxis-mcp.spec's datas or ship it in the signed artifact. Every description below is written in our own words after reading PLAXIS's official command reference locally installed with the product; no text is copied verbatim from that Bentley-copyrighted documentation, per CAROS_PLAXIS_MCP_COMPATIBILITY_PLAN.md and the vendor-redistribution gate in scripts/write_artifact_manifest.py.
note_on_other_generations: Every entry here is scoped to legacy-38 (V22) only. Nothing is assumed to hold for current-312 (PLAXIS 2024.2+) or legacy-37 (V21) until those installs are live-tested, per the rollout order in CAROS_PLAXIS_MCP_COMPATIBILITY_PLAN.md. Add new tagged entries after verifying against those installs; do not edit this file's runtime_profile to broaden its claimed scope.

commands.our_summary: Saves the project, optionally to a new path. There is no separate 'saveas' -- one command handles both.
commands.notes: Originally implemented against a nonexistent 'saveas' method; fixed in WP-A of the enrichment plan.

commands.our_summary: Creates a new phase relative to an existing one: phase() places it after, insertphase() places it before. Neither has a zero-argument form; InitialPhase always exists as the anchor for the first real phase.
commands.argument_shape: phase(reference_phase) or insertphase(reference_phase) -- reference_phase must be a resolved Phase object, not its name
commands.notes: Was entirely unwired before this session; only reading existing phases was possible.

commands.our_summary: Makes an existing phase current for further edits.

Activates or deactivates one or more objects in one or more phases. The sequence-form signature takes two lists (objects, phases), each serialised by plxscripting as a parenthesised group -- this is the form we use, not the single-object variadic-phases form.
commands.argument_shape: activate(objects: list, phases: list) -- both lists of resolved objects, passed as two list arguments

commands.our_summary: Calculates phases. With no arguments, calculates every phase currently marked for calculation, handling dependency order (e.g. InitialPhase before a phase that follows it) automatically. With explicit phases, calculates exactly those phases, variadic (not a parenthesised sequence) -- calculate(Phase_1, Phase_6), not calculate([Phase_1, Phase_6]).
commands.argument_shape: calculate() or calculate(*phases) -- star-unpacked, opposite calling convention from activate
commands.notes: Live-verified: calculate(Phase_1) alone fails if InitialPhase (its start phase) has not itself been calculated; calculate() with no arguments resolves that ordering on its own.

commands.our_summary: Sets one property of an object for one specific phase only (distinct from a plain, non-phase-scoped property set). Called as a method on the target object being modified, not on the global object -- the phase is the middle positional argument.
commands.notes: setproperties also has non-phase-scoped and multi-property-pair forms not implemented here; set_property (via plain attribute assignment) already covers the simple case.

commands.our_summary: Switches the Input working mode. gotosoil and gotostructures take no parameters. gotomesh, gotowater, and gotostages additionally accept an optional force-new-intersection Boolean -- passing it for soil/structures is a client-side error, not silently ignored. gotostages (and by extension gotomesh/gotowater) requires at least one polygon to already exist in the geometry.
commands.argument_shape: gotoX() or gotoX(force_new_intersection: bool) for mesh/water/stages only
commands.notes: Live-verified: setmaterial's basic form additionally requires Soil/Geometry mode specifically, not just 'not Stages mode' -- discovered while completing the calculate proof, not documented explicitly in setmaterial's own page.

commands.our_summary: Generates a mesh, optionally with a relative element size factor and enhanced refinement flag. enhanced_refinement requires the size factor to also be given -- there is no signature for enhanced_refinement alone.
commands.argument_shape: mesh() or mesh(size: float) or mesh(size: float, enhanced_refinement: bool)
commands.notes: Live-verified: produced a real mesh (240 elements, 2013 nodes) on a two-borehole disposable fixture.

commands.our_summary: Creates one or more points at literal (x, y) coordinates. Unlike line/polygon, point never accepts an existing-object reference for its own arguments.
commands.argument_shape: point(*coordinate_pairs) -- variadic, each pair a literal (x, y) tuple

commands.our_summary: Creates a line (2 vertices) or a polyline (3+ vertices) through a mix of existing Point references and literal (x, y) coordinates. A third signature supports an angle/relative/vector sub-command mini-language for lines defined by direction and length; that signature is not implemented.
commands.argument_shape: line(*vertices) -- variadic, each vertex either a resolved Point object or a literal (x, y) tuple
commands.notes: Only the vertex-list form is implemented, by design (documented as a limitation in the tool description).

commands.our_summary: Creates a polygon from 3 or more vertices, each either an existing Point reference or a literal coordinate. A second signature builds a polygon from Polycurve objects instead; not implemented, since it depends on a polycurve command this catalog does not wire.
commands.argument_shape: polygon(*vertices) -- variadic, same vertex union as line
commands.notes: Live-verified: two boreholes with matching soil layers auto-generate a soil polygon without this command being called directly -- create_polygon is for standalone geometry, not borehole-derived soil.

commands.our_summary: Adds a borehole at a given x-coordinate.
commands.argument_shape: borehole(x: number) -- x may be negative or zero; it is a coordinate, not a magnitude

commands.our_summary: Adds a soil layer with a given height, stacked under the previously added layer within the current borehole context.

Creates a material set of the given kind. All five share one identical shape: a zero-argument form that creates an unusable placeholder, and a free-form name/value property-pairs form. Material constitutive models are not individually schema'd here (10+ models, dozens of parameters each); property names must match PLAXIS's own (e.g. 'SoilModel', 'gammaUnsat').
commands.notes: Confirmed identical across all five by reading platemat's page in full and grepping the other three's signature notation, not by assuming after the first match.

commands.our_summary: Assigns a material to one or more features. The basic 'one or more features' signature already covers a single feature (its own minimum count is 1), so a single-feature call and a multi-feature call use the same code path -- no branching on count. Phase-scoped assignment signatures exist but are not implemented here.
commands.argument_shape: setmaterial(features: list, material) -- features always passed as one list argument
commands.notes: Live-verified requirement not stated on this page: the basic form is scoped to Soil/Geometry mode and fails with an opaque error in other modes.

commands.our_summary: Adds a structural element feature to one or more existing lines. All four share an identical first signature; each command also has several more overloads (create-from-points, inline material assignment, etc.) that are not implemented -- only the add-to-existing-line form.
commands.argument_shape: plate(*lines) -- variadic, each line a resolved Line (or Polycurve) object
commands.notes: Confirmed identical first signature by reading each command's page individually, not assumed after plate's first match.

commands.our_summary: Returns the full result table for a phase, result type, and fem_type ('node', 'stresspoint', 'element', or 'materialpoint' -- exactly these four), with an optional trailing smoothing Boolean. Also has entity-scoped and centerline-scoped signatures, not implemented; those need get_results extended with an entity/centerline argument in a future pass.
commands.notes: Live-verified against 50,370 real result values with correct lossless paging.

commands.our_summary: Returns one result value at a named curve point or a literal (x, y) coordinate, each with an optional trailing smoothing Boolean -- four of the page's six signatures. The remaining two (a directional vector for smoothing, and an updated-mesh-geometry coordinate lookup) are not implemented.
commands.argument_shape: getsingleresult(phase, result_type, point) or getsingleresult(phase, result_type, x, y), each optionally with a trailing smoothing bool

commands.our_summary: A flat, 16-category object (Soil, Plate, Interface, ...), each drilling one level further into the actual leaf result-type names. The existing safe_dir/describe_value-based listing already surfaces this shape correctly with no gaps -- verified by reading the object reference and confirmed by listing both the root and ResultTypes.Soil live.
commands.argument_shape: n/a -- read via ordinary path resolution, not a command call
